glosses: A girl or an unmarried young woman.

examples.text: She's unmarried and still a maiden.

glosses: A man with no experience of sex, especially because of deliberate abstention.

examples.text: As for that ſaid ſire Bors I wille be ſhryuen with a good wylle / Soo ſyr Bors was confeſſyd / and for al wymmen ſir Bors was a vyrgyne / ſauf for one / that was the doughter of kynge Brangorys / and on her he gat a child that hyghte Elayne / and ſauf for her ſyre Bors was a clene mayden[…]
examples.translation: As for that, said Sir Bors, I will be shriven with a good will. So Sir Bors was confessed, and for all women Sir Bors was a virgin, save for one, that was the daughter of King Brangoris, and with her he begat a child that hight Elaine, and save for her Sir Bors was a clean maiden.
examples.english: As for that, said Sir Bors, I will be shriven with a good will. So Sir Bors was confessed, and for all women Sir Bors was a virgin, save for one, that was the daughter of King Brangoris, and with her he begat a child that hight Elaine, and save for her Sir Bors was a clean maiden.

glosses: An unmarried woman, especially an older woman.
A racehorse without any victory, i.e. one having a \"virgin record\".
A horse race in which all starters are maidens.
A Scottish counterpart of the guillotine.

examples.text: It had been customary during the whole civil war, to decapitate state criminals by the instrument called the maiden; but Montrose was condemned to a more ignominious death , by a gibbet thirty feet high

glosses: Like or befitting a (young, unmarried) maiden.

examples.text: Haue you no modeſty, no maiden ſhame, / No touch of baſhfulneſſe?

glosses: Being a first occurrence or event.

examples.text: 1975 was the year when West Indies won their maiden World Cup title.
The Titanic sank on its maiden voyage.

After Edmund Burke's maiden speech, William Pitt the Elder said Burke had "spoken in such a manner as to stop the mouths of all Europe" and that the Commons should congratulate itself on acquiring such a member.
Venezuelan Pastor Maldonado took his maiden victory and Williams's first since 2004 in a strategic battle with Ferrari's Fernando Alonso.

glosses: Being an over in which no runs are scored.

examples.text: He bowled a record twelve maiden overs in his spell of 8-33 in 21 overs.

glosses: Fresh; innocent; unpolluted; pure; hitherto unused.

examples.text: Come Brother Iohn, full brauely haſt thou fleſht thy Maiden ſword.

When I am dead, good Wench, / Let me be vs’d with Honor; ſtrew me ouer / With Maiden Flowers, that all the world may know / I was a chaſte Wife, to my Graue: Embalme me, / Then lay me forth (although vnqueen’d) yet like / A Queene, and Daughter to a King enterre me.

glosses: Never having been captured or violated.

examples.text: Victorie forsook him for ever since he ransacked the maiden town of Magdenburg

glosses: Grown from seed and never pruned.

glosses: Jeune femme, demoiselle, indistinctement de son statut nobiliaire ; le mot, pour le sens et l’usage familier, a sans doute correspondu à notre actuel ma petite dame.

examples.text: Il n’y a plus de Damoiselles en France ; on dit maintenant Demoiselle d’une marchande de pommes. Nous manquons absolument de termes distinctifs pour l’âge, pour l’état, pour les conditions, pour ce que réclamerait sans doute l’intérêt des mœurs et de l’honnêteté publiques.
